 Once Upon a Farm Recalls Tractor Wheels Toddler Snacks Due to Choking Hazard
 The FDA has issued a safety advisory, and the company will reformulate the product after three choking incidents
 By 
 Jessica D’Argenio Waller, MS, CNS, LDN, CPST 
 Baby & Health Writer 
 November 3, 2026 
 Photo: Once Upon A Farm
 The baby food company Once Upon a Farm is recalling all flavors and packages of its Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars after three reports of toddlers choking on the soft, circular bars. The Food and Drug Administration issued a safety advisory about the product, warning consumers not to buy or serve the snack bars and telling retailers not to sell them.
 “The FDA has received several reports that describe toddlers (ages 1.5–2.5 years) suffering complete airway obstruction with the inability to breathe after consuming the product,” the advisory says. “When chewed, the product reportedly forms a dry, sticky mass that standard choking interventions—including back blows and the Heimlich maneuver—may fail to dislodge. Some reported choking incidents have required emergency response intervention and hospital observation.”

 The soft-baked bars are made from oat flour, dates, and pumpkin seed butter, and include other fruits and vegetables. Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels were sold online and in stores nationwide, including Costco, Target, and Walmart. 
 The FDA says the product may also be sold elsewhere, including on Amazon and through third-party vendors. The bars come in three flavors: Apple, Sweet Potato, & Spinach; Strawberry, Pumpkin, & Beet; and Banana, Pumpkin & Cauliflower. All flavors, all lots, and all package sizes are being recalled. 
 In a statement on the company’s website , Once Upon a Farm says it received three reports of choking and initiated a voluntary recall. The company says it’s working with the FDA “to make sure affected products are removed and families have the information they need.”
 “We know that parents place their trust in us every time they buy one of our products. We fell short of that, and that is why we are taking these aggressive actions,” the company statement says.   
 John Foraker, co-founder and CEO of Once Upon a Farm, said in a statement that in evaluating Tractor Wheels, the company was “reformulating these family favorites to ensure they adhere to the highest standards.” No other Once Upon a Farm products are affected by this recall. 
 Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels Recall Details
 Products recalled: All Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels Organic Soft-Baked Bars.
 Affected lots and varieties: All flavors, quantities, varieties, and all lots and expiration dates. 
 Flavors: 
 Apple, Sweet Potato, & Spinach Tractor Wheels  
 Strawberry, Pumpkin, & Beet Tractor Wheels  
 Banana, Pumpkin & Cauliflower Tractor Wheels  
 The problem: Tractor Wheels soft-baked bars are round, wheel-shaped biscuits that reportedly form a dry, sticky mass when chewed that standard choking interventions may fail to dislodge. The Food and Drug Administration has received three reports of toddlers between the ages of 1.5 and 2.5 choking on the bars and suffering complete airway obstruction, with some children receiving emergency care and needing hospital observation.
 What to do next: Don’t buy or serve Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels, and throw away the product. Return the product (even if opened), or bring your proof of purchase to the original purchase location for a full refund. You may also contact care@uponafarm.com for more information.
 High-Risk Choking Foods for Young Children
 Hot dogs (especially cut into a coin shape), sausages, and fish with bones. 
 Popcorn, chips, pretzel nuggets, and similar snack foods. 
 Candy (especially hard or sticky candy), cough drops, gum, lollipops, marshmallows, caramels, hard candies, and jelly beans. 
 Whole grapes, raw carrots (cut into rounds), and cherries. 
 Peanut butter (especially in spoonfuls or with soft white bread). 
 Foods that clump, are sticky, or dry and hard-textured. 
 Jessica D’Argenio Waller, MS, CNS, LDN, CPST
 Jessica D’Argenio Waller is a baby and health writer and editor at Consumer Reports, covering a range of topics, from strollers to infant formula to safe sleep practices. Before joining CR in 2025, she was editorial director at Motherly. Jessica is a licensed and board-certified nutritionist and a certified child passenger safety technician, a mom of two, and an avid runner and home cook.
